artists.biography: Electronic were an alternative dance supergroup formed by New Order singer and guitarist Bernard Sumner and ex-Smiths guitarist Johnny Marr. They co-wrote the majority of their output between 1989 and 1998, collaborating with Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe, of the Pet Shop Boys, on three tracks in their early years, and former Kraftwerk member Karl Bartos on nine songs in 1995.

perplexity.description:
Electronic, the self-titled debut album by the British supergroup Electronic, was released on 28 May 1991. The band consisted of Bernard Sumner (of New Order) and Johnny Marr (of The Smiths), who combined their backgrounds in alternative rock and post-punk with electronic dance music elements. The album blends synthesizer-driven electronic music with rock guitar textures, creating a hybrid sound that was innovative for its time. It features a mix of emotional lyrical content and danceable beats, with notable singles like "Get the Message" and "Feel Every Beat" showcasing this fusion.

This album marked a significant point in both artists' careers, as it allowed them to explore a more commercial and accessible sound while maintaining artistic integrity. The collaboration also included contributions from Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe of Pet Shop Boys on some tracks, further enriching the electronic pop dimension. Critically, Electronic was well received for its fresh sound and songwriting, and commercially it achieved success with over a million copies sold worldwide. It established Electronic as a notable act in the early 1990s alternative dance and rock scenes, setting the stage for their subsequent releases.

Released on the Factory label in the UK and Warner Bros. internationally, the album runs approximately 47 to 52 minutes depending on the edition. It was recorded between late 1989 and early 1991, primarily in Manchester. The album's style is characterized by a seamless integration of analogue synth programming and Marr's distinctive guitar work, reflecting both artists' strengths and the era's evolving music technology. This debut remains a landmark for its successful melding of electronic and rock genres during a period when such crossovers were still emerging.
